output.title: Credential rotation is a workflow cost, not just a security topic
output.body:
If you run a small business, credential rotation usually shows up as plain workflow friction. An API key expires, a SaaS password changes, or an admin token gets reset, and someone has to re-enter it before a report, integration, or login starts working again. The real cost is not abstract. It is the time spent noticing the break, tracing what changed, and fixing it by hand.

That is also why AI is not the first question here. Credential rotation is mainly a systems and access-management problem, not a judgment task. AI can sit around the edge of the process, for example in alert routing or change notes, but the workflow still depends on how credentials are stored, updated, and checked. Any secrets-management or integration-refresh option is an infrastructure choice, not a Bareni capability or deployment.

The practical next step is simple: list the integrations and accounts you still rotate manually, then count how many times in a typical month someone has to re-enter or update a credential. Pick one recent failure and write down how long it took to notice and repair. That gives you a clean baseline for deciding whether to keep the manual process, buy a tool, or redesign the workflow. No drama, just a useful list.
